correctness.rationale: Define sign at the first zero hit during an active gating interval. The strong Markov generator yields a coupled two-state backward equation with active right/left values zero/one and inactive C1 transmission. A bounded eigenmode solution with forced zero positive-side reset mode explicitly gives p_A, p_I and stationary p_-. Uniform positivity of successful reset epochs gives eventual absorption and uniqueness. Strict resetting monotonicity and fixed-inactive-fraction switching-speed monotonicity follow from explicit derivatives with rigorously negative sign, while the fixed-distance and boundary-layer limits follow directly by controlled asymptotics. The delivered standalone program verifies 135 generator/boundary/limit consistency checks and four independent Brownian-bridge simulation comparisons; finite tests do not substitute for the infinite analytical proof.

value.rationale: The same transparent-target paper explicitly presents capture-side fraction as a simulation-only diagnostic, so a closed formula for it resolves a naturally prompted quantity. The exact sign-vs-resetting and sign-vs-gate-frequency laws quantify how two competing interventions affect which side is visited at detection; the finite fast-gate opposite-side probability demonstrates a nontrivial observable discontinuity despite ordinary FPT convergence. The high-reset distance boundary layer describes a physically meaningful crossover and requires no arbitrary parameter slice.
